subject: Partial response truncation impacting hosted text endpoint
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Susan Park <susan@northlane.ai>, NorthLane Eng <eng-lead@northlane.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Partial response truncation impacting hosted text endpoint

Hi Susan / NorthLane team,

We detected a problem this morning where responses from our hosted text-generation endpoint (model: rwd-large-v2) were getting truncated—customers reported partial outputs that abruptly stop around ~250–300 tokens. We're investigating and I wanted to alert you immediately rather than wait for a full postmortem.

Impact:
- A subset of requests to the hosted text endpoint in us-west-1 returned incomplete generations between ~07:45–08:05 PDT.
- Your app (NorthLane) saw ~12% of calls during that window return truncated responses.

What we're doing now:
- Engineers are investigating kernel scheduler and KV cache interactions that could drop continuation tokens.
- We've rerouted a percentage of traffic to a fallback variant (rwd-large-v2-stable) which should yield full responses; that change is rolling now.

Immediate ask: can you queue any high-volume batch runs for a few hours if possible? This will help us avoid noisy retries while we confirm the fix.

Attachments: brief incident logs and an initial traces screenshot for your ops team (incident_logs.txt, grafana_traces.png).

I'll update you with a timeline and full root cause as soon as we have confirmation. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

— Jonas
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Susan Park <susan@northlane.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-29T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial response truncation impacting hosted text endpoint

Thanks for the heads-up, Jonas.

Questions: Do you have an ETA for the rollback being fully applied? Our ingest pipeline has backpressure logic that may retry and duplicate conversations if we see many partial responses — any recommended temporary headers or flags we should set on requests to avoid duplicate processing?

Appreciate the quick update.

— Susan
Head of Integrations, NorthLane AI
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@northlane.ai>
Date: 2027-06-29T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Partial response truncation impacting hosted text endpoint

Connor / team — forwarding customer note and initial traces. Key facts:
- Observed truncated outputs correlate with a kernel selector change deployed in the last maintenance window (06:30 PDT) that aimed to improve throughput.
- Truncation appears when sequence length exceeds ~240 tokens and when KV cache eviction happens mid-generation.

Attachments: incident_logs.txt (filtering by request ids), grafana_traces.png showing p95 contiguity drop.

Action items I propose:
1) Immediately rollback selector change for the affected fleet in us-west-1 and confirm no regressions.
2) Add a short-term guard in the serving layer to reject requests that would cross the problematic path with a 429 / user-visible advisory rather than returning truncated output.
3) Postmortem + follow-up mitigation (kernel selector validation + unit test for mid-sequence KV eviction).

Also looping in Marissa for customer comms and Evelyn for postmortem scheduling.

— Jonas
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@northlane.ai>
Date: 2027-06-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial response truncation impacting hosted text endpoint

Thanks — we've rolled back the kernel selector change for the us-west-1 serving pool at 09:50 PDT. Early validation shows full continuation for previously affected requests.

Root cause (preliminary): a race between the new kernel's prefetch routine and the KV cache eviction signal causing the backend to prematurely conclude generation. This only triggered when the token generation path crossed a cache eviction boundary (roughly >240 tokens) and under specific batching patterns.

Mitigations applied:
- Rollback completed (09:50 PDT).
- Applied a temporary guard that fails fast for requests that would match the eviction pattern (used to avoid returning partial outputs).
- Flagged the kernel selector change for extended canary and added a regression test simulating mid-sequence evictions.

Next steps:
- We'll produce a full postmortem and timeline by EOD tomorrow.
- Recommend customers avoid high-volume long-sequence batch jobs for the next 24 hours while we complete the canary and tests.

Connor
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Susan Park <susan@northlane.ai>, NorthLane Eng <eng-lead@northlane.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-29T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Incident resolved: partial response truncation (update and next steps)

Hi Susan / NorthLane team,

Quick update: the rollback completed and verification shows responses for the affected traffic now return full continuations. We have stopped short of a full public postmortem while engineering completes the regression tests, but wanted to provide the interim resolution and next steps:

Summary:
- Incident window (us-west-1): 2027-06-29 07:45–09:50 PDT.
- Customer impact (NorthLane): ~12% of calls during the window returned truncated responses; there were no data leaks or other integrity issues.

What we changed:
- Rolled back kernel selector change at 09:50 PDT.
- Implemented a short-term guard to fail-fast rather than returning partial outputs.
- Added tests and extended canary for the selector change; plan to re-introduce only after additional regression coverage.

Recommended customer actions:
- If you see retries in your pipeline, we recommend deduplication using request IDs for jobs sent between 07:30–10:00 PDT and avoid reprocessing until confirmed.
- If you prefer, we can flag any suspicious request IDs on our side and provide a report — let us know and we'll prioritize.

We will share a full postmortem (root cause, timeline, code pointers, and long-term mitigations) by 2027-06-30 EOD. Thank you for your patience — and sorry again for the disruption.

Best,
Jonas Weber
On behalf of the Serving Runtime & Reliability team
Redwood Inference
